ic_name: TIA/EIA-485 (RS-485 via TI SLLA272C Design Guide)

spec_provided_observability.name: Differential bus voltage V_AB
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Direct measurement on an oscilloscope between line A and line B; should swing > ±1.5 V at the driver with 54-ohm load.

spec_provided_observability.name: Common-mode bus voltage (V_A+V_B)/2
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Should stay within -7 V to +12 V relative to receiver ground; excursions indicate GPD problems.

spec_provided_observability.name: Receiver output R / RO
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Logic-level reflection of bus state; observable on the host UART RX pin.

spec_provided_observability.name: Driver enable DE pin
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Probe to confirm timing of driver tri-state vs assert vs idle gap.

spec_provided_observability.name: Bus eye diagram
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Persistence-mode scope capture across many bits — opening width / height directly correlates with jitter budget and BER.

spec_provided_observability.name: Loss-of-signal LED / register bit (transceiver-specific)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Some modern transceivers expose a LOS / Bus-Activity status pin or register bit.

test_debug_features: Internal node loopback — drive DE=1 + RE#=0 on a single isolated node to TX+RX through itself (without other drivers active).
Bus contention detection — capture V_AB at the loopback receiver while transmitting; mismatch between TX D and RX R indicates external bus contention.
Failsafe verification — disable all drivers and confirm receiver R stays HIGH (mark) via internal or external failsafe biasing.
Termination integrity check — measure DC resistance between A and B with all drivers tri-stated; should equal R_T / 2 = 60 ohm for 120-ohm-terminated bus.
Stub-reflection inspection — single-shot scope capture of the rising edge; visible reflections indicate too-long stubs (L_stub > tr × v × c / 10).
interrupt_request: RS-485 has no protocol-level interrupt. Transceiver-level fault outputs (overheating, bus-fault) are vendor-specific and not part of the standard.
notes: RS-485 is an electrical / wire-level standard and does not specify DFT / scan / BIST. Conformance testing is conducted at the chip level (driver/receiver electricals) and at the system level (eye-diagram + BER vs cable length). Industry test suites for higher-level protocols built on RS-485 (Modbus conformance, DL/T645 conformance) test the link layer separately.
